name: UL Solutions Inc.
moat_justification: UL mark and accreditation make certification close to a market-access requirement in core North American safety categories; ROIC proxy 23.6%/28.5%/26.3% (2023-2025) and gross margin rising 47.9% to 49.5% prove pricing power, but global TIC share is only ~7% against larger SGS/Bureau Veritas/Intertek rivals and growth is structurally mid-single-digit.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality TIC franchise, moat 7/10 — but at $73.31 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 6.1%, IV@15% $19.48); it clears 15% only at ~$19.48.
moat_for: Regulatory/accreditation moat — UL mark embedded in codes and regulator/retailer requirements
Re-certification switching costs for manufacturers mid-product-cycle
ROIC proxy 24-28% sustained (2023-2025) with gross margin rising to 49.5%
Demand tied to non-discretionary safety regulation plus electrification, energy storage and AI-data-center build-outs
moat_against: Only ~7% global TIC share; smaller than SGS and Bureau Veritas at global scale
Standards-setting sits with the nonprofit parent, not the listed company
Demand follows customer product-development cycles (tariff/macro freezes hit volumes)
Controlled company — UL Standards & Engagement held 95.7% of voting power at Dec 31, 2024
Virtual/AI-assisted testing could commoditize low-complexity work
